_doc: The closure ledger (campaign spec 2026-08-31-reforge-full-campaign-design.md, S1.1/S1.3/S5; contract X2). One row per in-scope subsystem and per headless catalog tool. Canonical row list: reforge/ledger/rows.ts. Validate: npx tsx ledger/check.ts. Every wave child updates its rows in its landing commit; pin bumps flip touched rows to 'stale'.

rows.title: Tool result formatters (Read, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Write, task family)
rows.note: TEN of the graph's 44 `mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam` methods are excised and delegated to reforge-owned modules (Write, Glob, TaskCreate from M3-B; Read, Edit, Bash, Grep, TaskGet, TaskList, TaskUpdate from C4/W1), 6,568 minified chars. Every one of the ten owned MODULES is standalone-complete and registered in engine-ts/modules/index.ts: it ships its own constants and pure helpers, and only typed ports cross the adapter (Read's WeakMap+clock staleness prefix and tab-separator gate, Bash's background output path and task-ack envelope/ending, TaskUpdate's two agent-team predicates). The SUBSYSTEM row nevertheless stays `spliced`, not `standalone-complete`: 34 formatters remain, so the family is not owned. Coverage is honest too — the corpus renders one of Read's six result arms, one of Grep's three and the plain stdout path of Bash's six, and never truncates a Glob result; the arms it cannot reach are graded by strangle/contracts.test.ts (135 checks). DEPENDENCY EDGES (§2.4), one per effectful-port capture that leaves this row: `tool/Read` — the Read formatter's staleness prefix is a module WeakMap keyed by the result object and populated inside the Read tool's CALL path, then rendered through a Date.now()-derived day count, so it is a side channel owned by Read's execution, not data this wave can own; `subsystem/bash-executor` — the Bash formatter's background output path reads the live outputPathBindings registry, and its task-ack envelope/ending reach the background-task machinery §1.1 files under the Bash executor; `subsystem/subagent-dispatch` — TaskUpdate's completion nudge is gated on the session's agent/team identity. Read's tab-separator capture is a feature gate, and gates are neither spliced nor excluded (§3.3), so it is a port with no edge.

rows.title: Tool-result validators (Edit's validateInput and its 19 siblings)
rows.note: Split out of §1.1's 'formatters + validators' row by C4 with measured evidence: the Edit tool's error results ("String to replace not found in file.", "File has not been read yet.", the stale-read and match-count messages) are NOT produced by `mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam`. They are returned by a sibling `async validateInput`, 3,317 minified chars against the formatters' 155-1,590, carrying filesystem reads, readFileState access, `tengu_edit_tool_stale_read` telemetry and gate reads — mostly `effectful-port` captures. It needs its own scenario (a deliberately missing `old_string`) and its own gate row, so C4 scoped it out rather than smuggling it in behind a formatter wave. 20 `validateInput` methods exist in chunk-fy12d89p.js. OPEN: this row is filed under C4 because that is the child that subdivided it, and C4 does not close it — the roadmap owes it a wave assignment (campaign spec Revision Notes, 2026-09-01).

rows.note: C5/W2 owns FOUR description functions and ONE satellite chunk whole. The row's charter is wider than that on purpose, and it is not met: chunk-y30v0ja7 is reforge-owned end to end (the campaign's first S-chunk: 3 exports, 0 upstream bytes), but the Read, Grep and WebFetch chunks carry 15/17/4 exports of unrelated behaviour -- PDF page-range parsing, the REPL registry, the deferred-tool policy, the WebFetch answering prompt -- and stay upstream's, so only their description functions are spliced. The catalog also has description functions beyond these four. 'standalone-complete' would therefore be an overclaim; every owned module IS standalone-complete individually and registered in engine-ts/modules/index.ts, which is what closes the dual-wiring half. Edges are the four typed ports the descriptions take from the graph: leanPrompt (system-prompt policy), subagentSteer (subagent dispatch, latching), pdfCapable (reads the session model, hence the query-loop row) and cacheTtlPhrase (the WebFetch cache TTL). Branch coverage: attestation/w2-descriptions.md.

rows.note: C1's free-function mechanism spike, kept as a permanent splice: the <env> block itself is owned, the surrounding system-prompt assembly is not. `spliced`, not `standalone-complete` — all nine interpolated values are `effectful-port` captures still supplied by the graph (cwd, git/OS reads, directory-context sections, platform). No edges recorded: those captures read process and session state rather than another ledger row's subsystem; C6 designs their ports. C4/W1 retrofit: the two model-description sections ($K/UK) are now owned outright rather than called on the graph, so the module is standalone-complete (only typed ports cross) and is registered in engine-ts/modules/index.ts. The SUBSYSTEM stays `spliced` — the <env> block is one function of W3's system-prompt assembly, not the assembly.

rows.title: Compaction: summarization prompt, compact_boundary emit, trigger policy
Hook dispatch + hooks chunks
rows.note: C5x's generator-shape spike owns the PostToolUse dispatcher (upstream b3e, executePostToolHooks): the hook-input record's field set and the executor's call contract. The other seven per-event dispatchers and the 23 KB shared executor (a port here, and S-module-shaped per the W5-W7 scout) remain W5's. Edges: the working-directory reader and the base hook-input builder, which reads session identity and app state.

rows.title: Permission decisions + rule matching/parsing
rows.note: C5x's arrow-initializer spike owns the chain's deny-stamping link (upstream kye, hasPermissionsToUseToolWithSink): a deny from the decision body is stamped with where it was decided, everything else passes through. The 11.6 KB mode-aware decision body it delegates to (von) stays a port and stays W6's — the W5-W7 scout measured it S-module-shaped. No outward edge: the port's far side is inside this same row.

rows.title: Moat tools: SendMessage/ListAgents, Workflow, ScheduleWakeup, TaskCreate family, Skill, plan/worktree tools
Session/transcript storage; resume/fork
rows.note: C1's class-method mechanism spike, kept as a permanent splice: one method of the transcript store (materializeSessionFile) is owned, the store is not. `spliced` — the store instance itself crosses as the delegation's receiver, which is exactly the `SessionPort` C12 will design. C4/W1 retrofit: the three pure error predicates (errorCode/isExpected/formatError) are now owned outright, so the module is standalone-complete behind its store/log/report ports and is registered in engine-ts/modules/index.ts. The SUBSYSTEM stays `spliced` — W9 owns the SessionPort.

rows.title: MCP adapter (thin layer over the vendored MCP SDK)
Query loop / turn driver (retry, 529, model fallback, compaction driver)
rows.note: C1's switch-case mechanism spike, kept as a permanent splice: the streaming assembler's text_delta arm is owned; retry, fallback and the compaction driver are not. `spliced` — the content block under assembly and the engine's telemetry plumbing cross as `effectful-port` captures. C4/W1 retrofit: no capture changed hands (the telemetry brands were already owned at W0a), but the module moved to the reference/sabotage layout and is registered in engine-ts/modules/index.ts, so both halves of dual-wiring now exist for it. The SUBSYSTEM stays `spliced`: one delta arm is not the turn driver.
